title: Observability-driven migration retrofit notes
content:
Purpose:
This note collects field-observed heuristics and runbook fragments for migrating private deployments (VPC/on-prem) where we intentionally drive decisions from observability signals instead of purely time-based windows. It is a retrofit log from multiple customer cutovers in 2024–2025 and an emerging pattern we want to codify into a lightweight playbook and a set of Terraform safety snippets.

Scope and constraints:
- Applies to control plane and runtime version bumps that are backwards-compatible at the API surface but have behavioral changes (KV cache layout, batching heuristics, kernel selection differences).
- Assumes customer-managed networking and strict egress rules; therefore most probes are local to the deployment or run from a trusted probe subnet.
- Does NOT cover full data-migration (KV/DB schema) beyond what is required to enable runtime compatibility shims.

High level migration strategy (observability-driven):
1) Lab verification: small cluster replica with representative traffic replay. Capture baseline metrics (p50/p95 latency, token/sec, cache hit rate, error rate, kv-sync lag).
2) Silent shadow: route 0% production traffic but mirror traces and metrics; synthetic canary requests injected at the same rate as production feature flows.
3) Canary slice: 1–2% traffic with circuit breakers and short TTLs; monitor live signals.
4) Progressive ramp: increase traffic in geometric steps (1, 4, 16, 64%) with checks at each step driven by metric gates.
5) Cutover or rollback based on signal evaluation and safety nets (see Runbook below).

Recommended observability signals (gates):
- User-facing error rate: less than 0.05% increase over baseline (30m rolling).
- Latency p95: must not degrade more than 12% vs baseline for two consecutive evaluation windows (10m windows).
- Token generation throughput per-GPU: within +/-15% of baseline for non-burst windows.
- Cache hit rate (prefix/KV): no more than 8 percentage points drop.
- Trace-level anomaly rate: automated anomaly detector flag count increase < 2x.
- Backpressure and queue depth on ingress: must not increase above safe threshold defined per-customer (default: 2x steady-state).
- Silent errors (e.g., partial responses, truncated streams): zero tolerance during canary; any occurrence -> immediate rollback trigger.

Signal sources and probes:
- Synthetic probe templates: seed prompts, long-tail prompts, cold-start prompts, and forced-kv-miss cases. Keep them in repo: infra/probes/private-migration/
- Trace correlation: ensure both sides inject migration-tag header (X-RW-MIGRATION-ID) so traces from old and new runtimes can be correlated.
- Telemetry to collect: internal opentracing spans, runtime kernel selection logs, quantization fallback counters, and eviction profiles.

Terraform safety snippets (patterns we used successfully):
- State pinning and read-only mode for sensitive resources: before cutover, set sensitive modules to lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true } temporarily and do plan-only runs for dependent resources.
- Module pin file: create modules/locks.tf with module_version constraints; keep a rollback_version variable for quick re-pin.
- Plan-compare job: automated CI job that runs terraform plan against both control-plane and runtime modules and emits a JSON diff artifact; human must sign off for diffs touching networking or stateful sets.
- Preflight drift check: run terraform refresh and compare KV-config hashes; abort if drift > 0.
- Safe apply script: a wrapper that obtains a temporary lock in our internal deployment orchestration, applies, and stages a rollback snapshot (state snapshot + runtime image tag) to S3.

Example safe-apply checklist (to be automated but useful to read):
- Create pre-migration snapshot: export tfsate + runtime-config bundle.
- Run plan-compare; annotate JIRA ticket with the plan artifact.
- Run lab replay and attach sample traces.
- Ensure SLO gates are set in observability with alerting muted to the incident channel.
- Kick the canary slice and start timer.

Failure/recovery runbook (canary failure scenario):
Trigger: p95 latency exceeds threshold for two consecutive windows OR synthetic probe error appears.
Immediate steps (0–5m):
- Pause ramping job and hold traffic at last safe slice.
- Open incident channel and tag "migration-canary".
- Collect the following: runtime logs (last 15m), probe traces, plan diff, kernel-selection samples.
- If partial responses seen, switch canary traffic to fallback model variant (configured via route policy)
Escalation (5–20m):
- If root cause not identified within 15m, revert Terraform module pin to rollback_version and trigger safe-apply to restore state bundle.
- If immediate revert not possible, enable traffic diversion to hosted fallback for the affected API route.
Post-incident (20m+):
- Run postmortem template. Capture: exact metric deltas, trace ids, extracted stack frames, and remediation steps.

Compatibility adapter patterns observed in practice:
- Lightweight proxy shim: translate older API header/field names to new ones and vice versa. Best when the change is additive or purely renaming. Keep shim stateless and colocated on the same node pool as ingress.
- Feature-flagged behavior toggles: accept both old and new behaviors under a runtime flag; flip during canary after verifying observability gates.
- KV migration dual-write: write to both old and new KV keys for 24–72h and compare read consistency in shadow. Use a monotonically increasing verification token in writes.

What worked (lessons learned):
- Instrument probes that exercise the long tail of model behavior — many regressions only showed up on rare prompt shapes.
- Keep plan diffs small and human-reviewable. Large monolithic diffs cause hesitation and misconfiguration.
- Temp lifecycle prevent_destroy is a lifesaver for customers that disallow destructive changes during business hours.
- Correlating traces by migration-id reduces MTTR; set this as a required header for all migration jobs.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Can we standardize a minimal migration telemetry payload and make it a runtime export (so customers don’t need custom probes)?
- Should we add a terraform module that automatically creates a rollback snapshot bucket and retention policy? (Security team needs to sign off on S3 retention)
- How granular should the default gate thresholds be per-customer? Propose a small matrix: low-risk, medium-risk, high-risk profiles.

Action items (short term):
- Convert probe templates into a reusable 'migration-probes' module (owner: Diego).
- Draft an internal RFC for migration-id header and trace correlation (owner: Anya).
- Prototype a safe-apply wrapper in infra-scripts and add it to the private-deployments runbook (owner: Samira).

Appendix: quick commands and snippets (informal)
- Plan compare: 
  terraform init && terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform show -json tfplan > tfplan.json
- Snapshot state: 
  aws s3 cp terraform.tfstate s3://migration-state-snapshots/${ENV}/${TIMESTAMP}.tfstate
- Canary flip (via routing): 
  curl -X POST 
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' 
    -d '{"route":"/generate","percent":1,"tag":"migration-2026-02-03"}' 
    https://console.internal.redwood/api/v1/routes/update

Notes to self: keep this doc informal — we'll split into a polished playbook and a quick-run checklist once we've validated the prototype safe-apply script.
